source.repro: PIF_PATH=/path/to/hs1ToMm39.over.chain.pif.gz PIF_ASSEMBLIES=hs1,mm39 npx jest plugins/comparative-adapters/src/pifTierBytes — the test skips without PIF_PATH. The file is hosted at jbrowse.org/genomes/hs1_vs_mm39/ (HOSTING.md); it is 130 MB, so it is fetched rather than committed.
source.notes: Both tiers of ONE file, which is the comparison a reader experiences — `--no-coarse` against the default is a question about disk, and pif-coarse-tier-bytes answers that one. Bytes are counted by the local server the adapter fetches from, so they are what the socket carried rather than the size of the parsed rows; they came back byte-identical across runs. Every row of each tier is returned at this zoom, so `rows returned` is the whole tier. Index bytes (709 kB of .tbi) are excluded, being identical for both arms. Wall-clock is deliberately not a column: over loopback it is parse time, it moved 27% between two runs of the same arm, and a real time-to-settled wants a browser.
